reviews.evidence: v2.0.0 source review, internal/handler/auth_sessions.go:405 (sha256:764e8e9b3377f98dde687cb2941f2b65ebac89608cbd913c305694d645252b30): Session/refresh cookies use HttpOnly and Lax; CSRF token is intentionally script-readable. Secure comes from reqctx.RequestIsHTTPS, with production forced by internal/server/routes.go and trusted proxy metadata. Logout marker is a non-authoritative UX hint and now also uses the Secure resolver. Grafana cookie is HttpOnly/Strict and Secure for the configured HTTPS Astronomer URL. See internal/reqctx/request_test.go and handler session-cookie tests. HTTPS session/refresh/CSRF cookies now require __Host- names with no legacy fallback; session hint follows the same host boundary. BrowserCookie and ValidateCSRF boundary tests pass.

v2.0.0 browser isolation source review: internal/handler/service_proxy.go:142 (sha256:8f209ec1aa94f2992f3f35ca882918f9ae4d6da950e1d51b5c47728df61f2c0d). Downstream HTML is now reachable only through internal/toolui host dispatch and a target-bound encrypted session; old console routes emit owned launch HTML or 410/503. Dedicated proxy auth preserves RBAC, binds installed namespace, strips credentials and downstream cookie/CORS/security-policy overrides, rejects service workers, and cannot route to console APIs. Protected main/SSO cookies prevent sibling injection. Owning toolui/auth/grafanaproxy/handler/server tests pass, including actual-router launch/redeem, cross-origin rejection, grant replay, target confinement, RBAC denial and namespace controls. Independent review's SSO cookie finding was fixed and tests rerun. See docs/assurance/technology-guide/tool-ui-isolation-review.md and docs/runbooks/tool-ui-isolation.md. Live wildcard DNS/TLS acceptance remains a deployment gate, not claimed by this source disposition.

v2.0.0 source review, scripts/qualify-offerings/main.go:527 (sha256:8a3485e493987eafc31b2688bb58ae3cc4ef6e0b60007fbddd4a6dd26f81603e): Operator/qualification process execution uses executable plus separate argv via os/exec, not shell concatenation. The named path is selected by the local CLI/protected qualification runner; no HTTP request can choose executable text. Production process runner validates absolute paths, bounded captures/timeouts, and an explicit environment (internal/ops/process/process.go). Database publication signer executes a captured inode using /proc/self/fd/3 and explicit environment; distribution publication validates an absolute regular executable. Tool commands and qualification hooks require operator authority already equivalent to process launch.
